summary: A Financial Times commentary argues that the leaders of the United States, China and Russia are unable to dominate global affairs as a unified bloc, citing structural, strategic and domestic constraints that prevent them from carving up the world together.

headline: Nvidia shares fall after US restricts chip access to China
summary: Nvidia’s stock continued to decline after the US Commerce Department announced a rule limiting China’s remote access to advanced chips. The move follows harsh comments from the US government about the chipmaker’s ties to China, adding pressure on the company’s share price.

headline: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal after sexual assault conviction
summary: French actor Gérard Depardieu has withdrawn his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a Paris film set. In a written statement he accepted the verdict and apologised to the victims, confirming the court’s original ruling.

headline: Pakistan floods linked to intensified monsoon rainfall
summary: University lecturer Imran Lodhi describes how climate-driven intense monsoon rains caused devastating floods in Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan, displacing families and prompting urgent relief efforts.

headline: Rising shipping costs could limit holiday inventory
summary: Transport executives say higher freight rates are prompting retailers to curb stock of big-ticket holiday items, making some products harder to find for shoppers.

headline: UK’s oldest renewable projects set for £9bn subsidy windfall
summary: Analysis shows that legacy wind and solar farms in Britain could receive nearly £9 billion in payments next year as market prices surge, prompting calls to reform the subsidy scheme.

headline: Eurovision Asia footage edited in Malaysia over LGBTQ content
summary: The European Broadcasting Union says it will write to the Asian contest licence holder after Malaysia’s TV3 cut drag and gay jury footage from the first Eurovision Asia broadcast.

headline: Teen AFL hopeful Lucas Robinson eyes legend’s footsteps ahead of draft
summary: Prospective draftee Lucas Robinson reveals the Australian Football League great he wants to emulate as he prepares for this week’s national draft.

headline: Xi, Trump and Putin to meet in Shenzhen for trilateral talks
summary: China, the United States and Russia will hold a first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting in Shenzhen during the APEC summit, with leaders Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin expected to discuss world-peace topics such as denuclearisation.

headline: Israeli military uploads 3.5 million photos to Amazon cloud for facial-recognition analysis
summary: Leaked documents reveal Israel moved millions of images of Palestinians to Amazon’s cloud platform to use its facial-recognition tools during the Gaza conflict.

headline: Investor warns fame can undermine tech founders at Nvidia and Tesla
summary: A prominent shareholder argues that the celebrity status of CEOs at Nvidia and Tesla can negatively affect both personal lives and company performance.

headline: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
summary: Separate attacks in KwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng have killed 17 people, highlighting the country’s ongoing struggle with violent crime.

headline: Robert Irwin and sprinter Gout among Queensland’s Australian of the Year nominees
summary: Conservationist Robert Irwin and 2024 sprint champion Gout Gout join two other Queensland advocates as finalists for the state’s Australian of the Year awards.

headline: Two passengers trapped atop Perth ferris wheel after operator leaves early
summary: WorkSafe will investigate after a Perth ferris wheel operator departed before the ride finished, leaving two paying riders stranded at the top.

headline: NSW inquest hears birth keeper told mother of deceased baby to ‘go home and rest’
summary: Coroner’s court hears that a birth keeper advised a pregnant woman, whose baby later died, to return home despite urgent medical advice to seek emergency care.

headline: Four-year-old injured after car crashes into Perth daycare fence
summary: A vehicle struck the fence of a daycare centre in Perth, causing injuries to a four-year-old boy. Emergency services attended the scene and the child was taken for medical treatment. No further details on the driver or cause were provided.

headline: Inquest opened into police shooting of 16-year-old in Perth car park
summary: A coronial inquest has begun into the fatal police shooting of a 16-year-old boy, described as radicalised, at a Bunnings car park in Perth. The inquiry will examine the circumstances surrounding the incident and the actions of the officer involved.

headline: NSW Premier Minns drops underquoting reforms amid housing slump backlash
summary: New South Wales Premier Chris Minns has shelved proposed underquoting legislation that would have forced real-estate agents to disclose price expectations to buyers. The decision follows a slowdown in the housing market and strong opposition from Sydney agents.

headline: Cape Town baboon relocation to sanctuary sparks protests
summary: Authorities in Cape Town began moving a troop of 44 baboons from Simon’s Town to a wildlife sanctuary, prompting demonstrators to block the transport. Officials say the relocation is needed to reduce human-wildlife conflict, while locals oppose the capture.

headline: Queensland police review use of unofficial AI-powered app
summary: Queensland Police are examining the deployment of an unofficial AI-driven application used by frontline officers after concerns were raised about its governance and data handling. The review follows broader scrutiny of AI tools in public sector operations.

headline: Opinion piece links wartime leaks to technology insiders
summary: A commentary argues that recent leaks of sensitive information may be traced to technology experts, suggesting a new dimension to espionage in modern conflicts.

headline: WA Police investigate complaints about Labor MP’s alleged debts
summary: Western Australian police have received complaints concerning alleged debts of Labor MP Jagadish Krishnan. The force confirmed the matters are under investigation.

headline: Inquest probes deaths of four babies born at home in northern NSW
summary: A coronial inquest is examining the circumstances surrounding the deaths of four infants born at home in northern New South Wales, including a mother’s fear of being forced into a caesarean section if she sought hospital care.

headline: Conjoined twin girls born in remote PNG, possible treatment in Australia
summary: Medical teams in a remote part of Papua New Guinea have delivered conjoined twin girls, marking the country’s second such case in just over a year. Authorities are exploring the possibility of transferring the infants to Australia for specialised care.

headline: European banks adopt AI to cut routine work but profit impact unclear
summary: Banks across Europe are deploying artificial intelligence to automate routine tasks, redeploy staff and recruit technical talent. While the technology promises efficiency gains, its effect on overall profitability remains uncertain.

headline: Rare EF1 tornado touches down in Delaware, causing property damage
summary: An EF1 tornado struck the Salem Woods neighbourhood of Newark, Delaware, damaging roofs, windows and a hotel sign, and overturning a semi-truck on I-95. No injuries or fatalities were reported.

headline: Swans players Heeney and Warner train after police clearance
summary: Sydney Swans stars Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner resumed training with teammates at Centennial Park following their clearance by police in connection with a hotel-room incident earlier this year.

headline: IMF chief warns AI-linked circular financing reaches $1 trillion
summary: Kristalina Georgieva said that circular financing for AI companies has grown to just over $1 trillion, with two-thirds in debt, as investor enthusiasm cools and global economic risks rise.

headline: Kangaroos credit doubters for World Cup triumph
summary: Australian rugby league stars said criticism of their abilities motivated the team, which went on to win the World Cup, highlighting the role of external scepticism in their success.

headline: Inquest begins into Queensland island fire deaths
summary: A coronial inquest has started into the blaze that killed a father and five children on a small Queensland island in 2023, seeking to determine the cause of the tragedy.

headline: Rugby Australia vows to fight players’ union legal challenge
summary: CEO Phil Waugh described the players’ union’s pay and conditions case as an aggressive, costly and avoidable legal battle, confirming Rugby Australia will defend the matter in court.

headline: Government scores poorly on every performance metric
summary: A new poll shows the current Australian government lagging on all measured performance indicators, with cost of living remaining the top concern for voters for the fifth consecutive year.

headline: Australia issues 30-year bonds as yields rise
summary: The Treasury launched a 30-year sovereign bond offering weeks after multi-decade high yields, attracting strong demand from global investors seeking long-term Australian debt.

headline: Metrics takes over distressed property assets
summary: Non-bank lender Metrics placed two property developers into receivership and listed a foreclosed retail strip for sale as defaults in the sector continue to rise.

headline: Severe weather forces 104 Sydney Airport flight cancellations
summary: Adverse weather conditions at Sydney Airport led to major delays and the cancellation of 104 flights, disrupting travel plans for thousands of passengers.

headline: UK, allies urge Israel to speed humanitarian aid to Gaza
summary: The United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy called on Israeli authorities to allow rapid delivery of essential supplies, including 150,000 tents, to Gaza, saying restrictions at border crossings were hindering humanitarian assistance.

headline: Test cricket hopefuls miss final selection window
summary: With the New Zealand series squad imminent, prospects Sam Konstas and Jack Clayton failed to impress in the One-Day Cup, losing their last chance to earn a Test debut.

headline: Qantas travel disruptions strand island residents
summary: Passengers from Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands were left stranded on the mainland after Qantas cancelled multiple flights, prompting frustration among island communities.

headline: Opposition says key details omitted from Torrens-Darlington briefing
summary: Opposition figures claim the $15.4 billion Torrens to Darlington infrastructure project briefing left out critical information about a contractor later suspended over alleged bikie links.

headline: Judge’s Facebook posts not enough to overturn abuse ruling
summary: A court dismissed Stephen Fane Noga’s appeal against a verdict that found him liable for sexual abuse of a former student in the 1980s, ruling his social-media activity did not merit a reversal.

headline: Darwin Private Hospital to continue services after takeover delay
summary: The Northern Territory health minister urged patients to keep scheduled procedures at Darwin Private Hospital despite Calvary Health Care postponing its acquisition date.

headline: Greens weigh alternative 40% CGT discount proposal
summary: The Australian Greens are considering a simpler capital gains tax discount model proposed by teal MP Tim Spender, which could challenge the government’s current CGT reform plans.

headline: Lendlease faces investor scepticism over bond redemption plan
summary: Lendlease said its bond redemption was part of proactive capital management, but investors remain unconvinced. The company’s sticky covenant and unexpected move have raised concerns about its financial strategy and market confidence.

headline: Aboriginal teen becomes youngest world surfing champion
summary: An Australian Aboriginal teenager made history by winning the world surfing title, becoming the sport’s youngest champion. The achievement highlights the rising talent and diversity in Australian surfing.

headline: Authors and creators push back against AI copyright lobbying
summary: Australia’s government push to attract AI investment has sparked a campaign by authors, musicians and TV producers. The creative sector argues the policy favours AI firms and threatens copyright protections.

headline: Anti-hype pitch to back record-size IPO gains traction
summary: Dario Amodei’s low-profile approach is being used to support what could become the largest initial public offering. Clients have been told order sizes may be trimmed by about 40 per cent as the deal progresses.

headline: NSW police sexual misconduct allegations revealed in review
summary: A culture review of the NSW Police Force uncovered claims of sexual harassment and assault by officers against fellow uniformed staff. The findings have prompted calls for further investigation and reforms.

headline: Rare 16th-century ‘Book of Miracles’ to be auctioned for £1 million
summary: The ‘Book of Miracles’, a 16th-century manuscript depicting apocalyptic scenes such as five suns over Leipzig and blood rain in Rome, is set to be auctioned. Public institutions will have the first chance to bid.

headline: Sydney Airport flights disrupted after safety directive
summary: Airservices issued a safety directive that forced airlines to slow arrivals and increase spacing due to low cloud, resulting in 92 flight cancellations and 347 delays at Sydney Airport on Monday.

headline: Usman Khawaja discusses racism and mental health in cricket
summary: Australian cricketer Usman Khawaja opened up about experiencing racist stereotyping, his sense of belonging, and early mental-health struggles linked to cricket setbacks, expanding the conversation beyond the Sandpapergate controversy.

headline: UK Labour leader says Brexit has failed ahead of EU summit
summary: Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham will argue at the upcoming UK-EU summit that Brexit “has not worked” and propose a new deal with the EU, claiming it could raise Britain’s GDP by 0.4 per cent. The comments come amid renewed debate over the post-Brexit relationship.

headline: Victorian town opposes AI data centre at former quarry
summary: Residents of Miners Rest, Victoria, are campaigning against a proposed AI data centre slated for the town’s old quarry, fearing it would disrupt their quiet rural lifestyle.

headline: James Packer’s large Nvidia stake highlighted amid scandal
summary: Billionaire James Packer’s significant investment in Nvidia has come under scrutiny, with reports noting his broader exposure to the tech giant through his Firmus holdings.

headline: Tasmanian author demands apology from premier over Christmas backlash
summary: Best-selling parenting author Biddulph has called on Tasmania’s premier to issue an unreserved apology after a social-media storm over the state’s Christmas celebrations.

headline: Humm faces board battle as director resigns and activist seeks seat
summary: Non-bank lender Humm is in turmoil after a director’s resignation and activist investor Jeremy Raper’s push for a board seat, intensifying a power struggle between founder Andrew Abercrombie and top shareholder.

headline: NSW anti-slavery commissioner refers labour hire syndicate crimes to police
summary: The NSW Anti-slavery Commissioner has referred allegations that labour hire syndicates kidnapped and blackmailed migrant workers to police, highlighting concerns over exploitation in the state’s labour market.

headline: NSW shelves new real estate advertising rules
summary: The NSW government has abandoned planned reforms that would have required property agents to display selling prices or price ranges, cancelling the changes a day before they were to take effect.

headline: PIMCO warns of sustained diesel shortage in Australia
summary: Asset manager PIMCO says the fallout from the US-Iran crisis could lead to a prolonged diesel crunch in Australia, urging an “all-energy” approach to meet rising demand.

headline: Severe thunderstorms bring snow-like hail to southern Queensland
summary: Heavy thunderstorms across southern Queensland produced hail up to 10 cm in size and wind gusts of 91 km/h, prompting warnings for residents in the affected areas.

headline: Jackdaw gas field receives UK government approval
summary: UK ministers have given the green light for gas production at the Jackdaw field, located 150 miles east of Aberdeen, after years of regulatory uncertainty.

headline: Court hears DNA link to Adelaide paediatrician murder suspect
summary: During a hearing, DNA matching murder-accused Kerem Aydin was reportedly found at the scene where Adelaide paediatrician Michael Yung was killed in 2023.

headline: Statue unveiled to honour Merle Thornton’s 1965 protest
summary: A new statue in Brisbane commemorates Merle Thornton, who chained herself to a bar in 1965 to protest the ban on women in Queensland public bars.

headline: Proposed on-shore gas bill faces constitutional challenge
summary: The coalition and Greens oppose a new bill that would require LNG exporters to supply a greater share of gas to Australian consumers, citing constitutional concerns.

headline: NRL highlights to be free for podcasters from 2028
summary: From 2028, podcasters covering the NRL will be allowed to use footage and highlight reels from Nine and Foxtel at no cost, subject to certain conditions.

headline: Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell remembered after death
summary: Former Beaconsfield miner Todd Russell was remembered for his humour and reflections on his funeral plans, recalling a previous burial he did not enjoy.

headline: Forrestania secures 72.5% stake in Zenith Minerals
summary: Forrestania Resources has completed a takeover offer, acquiring a 72.56 per cent controlling interest in Zenith Minerals. The deal advances Forrestania’s strategy to consolidate gold assets in Western Australia and brings Zenith under its operational umbrella.

headline: Australians at forefront of global AI safety efforts
summary: Dozens of Australians have relocated to San Francisco to work for leading AI labs or the surrounding AI safety ecosystem. They are actively raising concerns about the risk of artificial intelligence systems becoming uncontrolled.

headline: Gateway Mining reports high-grade gold find at Yandal project
summary: Gateway Mining announced a shallow, high-grade gold discovery at its Yandal project near Wiluna, Western Australia. Recent reverse-circulation drilling returned 11 metres at 4.5 g/t gold from 89 metres depth, confirming a new mineralised system.

headline: Westfield seeks new anchors as David Jones administrators meet creditors
summary: The owner of Westfield shopping centres has intensified pressure on administrators of David Jones, with meetings scheduled with creditors. Westfield is exploring replacement tenants for the department store’s locations across its Australian malls.

headline: UK ministers warned weakening EV targets would hurt car industry
summary: Experts told UK ministers that diluting the zero-emission vehicle mandate would slow market growth, raise costs for consumers and undermine the country's net-zero objectives, potentially harming the domestic automotive sector.

headline: Home Office criticised for attempting to cancel Andreas Malm online talk
summary: The Home Office faced accusations of trying to block an online event featuring climate academic Andreas Malm. Hackney mayor Shadwell decried the move as an assault on free speech after the talk proceeded despite warnings.

headline: England plans reforms to expand appeals for special-needs support
summary: Proposed changes to England’s special-needs education system could give families new routes to appeal for additional school support, including ombudsman reviews, amid criticism that current reforms dilute legal protections.

headline: Police shooting of 16-year-old extremist and trial of ex-officer draws scrutiny
summary: A coronial inquest heard that 16-year-old James Hollands, who sent a jihad-related text, was shot by police after a knife attack. Former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, charged with double murder, faced cross-examination and later re-examination by his own barrister during the trial.

headline: Allens bolsters M&A practice hiring Hamilton Locke senior partner
summary: Allens has expanded its mergers and acquisitions team, bringing in senior partner Hamilton Locke from Hamilton Locke. The move follows the firm’s ongoing effort to grow its M&A and capital markets capabilities.

headline: Travis Auld steps down as Australian Grand Prix Corp CEO
summary: Travis Auld has resigned as chief executive of the Australian Grand Prix Corporation. He will not disclose his next employer or the location of his new role, and his departure comes ahead of the upcoming Formula 1 season.

headline: Police release CCTV footage of fatal drive-by shooting
summary: Detectives from the Logan Criminal Investigation Branch have released CCTV footage showing a blue Mazda 2 near Bryants Road at the time of a fatal drive-by shooting. The video is being circulated to aid the investigation and encourage anyone with information to come forward.

headline: Report flags dysfunction at Serpentine Jarrahdale council
summary: An independent monitor’s report on the Shire of Serpentine Jarrahdale highlights concerns over councillor behaviour and psychosocial safety. The findings suggest systemic issues within the council and call for reforms to improve governance and staff wellbeing.

headline: Health Minister Butler urges states to allow puberty blockers
summary: Health Minister Mark Butler has challenged states and territories that have banned puberty blockers for children to follow new national guidelines. He says the guidelines are based on medical consensus and that denying access could harm young people’s health.

headline: EU envoy urges Australian government to back trade pact
summary: The new EU ambassador said the bloc would consider climate-assurance requests if the Australian government proposes a win-win trade deal. He described the potential agreement as a “bloody good deal” and urged the Coalition to support the negotiations.

headline: AFR launches indices to broaden ASX investment view
summary: The Australian Financial Review has introduced a suite of indices designed to give a wider economic perspective on ASX opportunities. The launch is positioned as the next step in strengthening Australia’s capital-markets infrastructure and supporting investors.

headline: Lucy Wicks responds to stalking allegations by MP Taylor Martin
summary: NSW MP Taylor Martin accused former staffer Lucy Wicks of stalking him in a parliamentary speech. Wicks has now publicly replied, denying the claims and defending her conduct amid the political dispute.

headline: Rex posts losses as US owner fails to restore fleet
summary: Regional airline Rex reported a loss after its US owner, tasked with returning planes to service, has not added a single aircraft in almost a year. The ongoing issues raise concerns about the airline’s expansion plans.

headline: Mother describes grief after son killed by 16-year-old
summary: A mother recounted the “unbearable” grief she feels after her son, Jack Westren, who had a brain injury, was ambushed and murdered by a group of teenagers at Shellharbour Junction train station.

headline: Sam Walker to discuss PNG Chiefs move with club officials
summary: Off-contract Roosters centre Sam Walker will meet PNG Chiefs officials on Tuesday to explore a potential transfer to the expansion franchise, where he could partner with Jarome Luai in the halves.

headline: Witness testimony ends in Lamarre-Condon court case
summary: The Crown prosecutor concluded the witness testimony of Beau Lamarre-Condon, reading statements from Jesse Baird’s brother and Luke Davies’s mother relating to evidence given by the accused, marking the end of that phase of the trial.

headline: Critical Resources gains access to high-grade antimony prospect
summary: Critical Resources has secured ground access to its Mayview antimony-gold prospect in NSW, where rock chip samples returned 52.3 % antimony, located just 2.7 km from the existing Hillgrove mine.

headline: Ken Wyatt appointed WA’s first Indigenous governor
summary: Former federal minister Ken Wyatt, the first Indigenous Australian elected to the House of Representatives, has been named Western Australia’s inaugural Indigenous governor, marking a historic first for the state.

headline: Albanese urged to boycott photo with Putin at APEC
summary: Critics have called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to avoid a photo-op with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit, warning it could normalise Russia’s standing and undermine Australia’s support for Ukraine.

headline: Judge rejects bid to keep Kmart child sex offender in prison
summary: A Queensland judge dismissed an application to keep a man convicted of child sexual offences at Kmart, allowing his release. The offender had lured a child from a mother in the toy aisle of a Westfield store in 2018. The decision follows legal arguments about his continued detention.

headline: Mother of five killed in Russell Island fire gives evidence at inquest
summary: A mother whose partner and five sons perished in a house fire on Russell Island has begun testifying at the inquest into the tragedy. She described the blaze as being everywhere and recounted the devastating loss of her family as investigators examine the cause of the fire.

headline: Australia joins US-led Pax Silica AI supply-chain pact
summary: Australia became a founding member of Pax Silica, a US-initiated alliance aimed at safeguarding AI supply chains from Chinese influence. The pact brings together seven countries to coordinate on rare-earth and semiconductor security, reflecting growing concerns over Beijing’s dominance in advanced technology components.

headline: Widow of Haiti’s assassinated leader registers for presidential race
summary: The wife of former Haitian president Jovenel Moïse, assassinated in 2021, has filed paperwork to run in the upcoming presidential election. Haiti has not held a national vote since the killing, and her candidacy marks a rare entry of a former first lady into the political arena.

headline: Independent MP Helen Haines discharged after hospitalisation
summary: Helen Haines, the independent MP who was attacked outside her office, has been released from hospital and entered the rehabilitation stage. She thanked supporters and donors for their messages and charity contributions. The attack resulted in double amputation of her legs, and she is now focusing on recovery.

headline: Barrenjoey tops broker survey as equities desks light up
summary: Barrenjoey Capital Partners was ranked first in the latest Peter Lee broker survey, outperforming peers across equity research and sales. The results highlight the firm’s strong performance on the Australian equities desk and its growing influence among institutional investors.

headline: Tax regulator pursues former KPMG manager over unauthorised GST refunds
summary: The Australian Taxation Office has launched action against Anthony George Confos, a former KPMG manager, for allegedly lodging unauthorised GST refunds and diverting nearly $1 million to personal accounts. The case underscores ongoing scrutiny of tax-avoidance schemes.

headline: Victorian premier says documents withheld from royal commission
summary: Premier Ben Carroll accused officials of withholding documents from the commission investigating the Big Build, while Health Minister Ingrid Stitt denied briefing claims. The dispute comes as the state government pushes free prenatal testing amid fears of an upcoming election loss.

headline: Former EY partner found to have promoted illegal tax schemes
summary: The Australian Taxation Office secured a court victory against former EY partner Peter White, who was found to have advised wealthy clients on unlawful tax structures. The ruling represents a significant enforcement action against professional misconduct in tax advisory services.

headline: UK ministers criticised for not knowing cost of NHS maternity repairs
summary: NHS chiefs warned that 43 percent of maternity and neonatal units in England fail to meet safety standards, accusing ministers of “gambling with safety” after admitting they lack knowledge of the repair costs for deteriorating facilities. The criticism highlights systemic infrastructure issues in the health system.

headline: Spain prepares for snap election that could bring far-right to power
summary: Spain will hold a snap general election on 29 November, its sixth in 11 years, with the possibility of a far-right party entering government for the first time since the Franco era. The vote could end eight years of socialist rule and reshape the political landscape.

headline: EU to propose €45 billion loan for Ukraine funded by EU budget
summary: The European Commission will present a proposal to lend Ukraine €45 billion, to be financed from the EU’s own budget. The loan aims to bridge Kyiv’s funding gap for the coming year and is part of the bloc’s broader support for the war-torn nation.

headline: Top 2026 IPOs tumble over 20% as AI hype fades
summary: The ten largest initial public offerings of the year have lost more than a fifth of their value on average, reflecting a slowdown in investor enthusiasm for artificial-intelligence driven companies after years of strong gains.

headline: Migration to rich nations slows sharply, adding fiscal strain
summary: A steep decline in the number of migrants arriving in wealthy countries is intensifying fiscal challenges linked to rapidly ageing populations, according to recent analysis.

headline: Australian accounting firms revamp fees as AI cuts billable hours
summary: Large Australian accounting practices are overhauling their fee structures because AI-driven automation is shortening compliance turnaround times and threatening traditional billable-hour revenue models.

headline: Labor backs gas reservation scheme for industrial users
summary: The Australian Labor Party supports the Domestic Gas Reservation Scheme, arguing it will give industrial consumers certainty of affordable, secure gas supplies over the long term.

headline: Mining funds retreat as AI-linked stock rally reverses
summary: Investors in mining-focused funds are moving to cash after a sharp reversal in the performance of stocks that had previously benefited from the artificial-intelligence trade.

headline: Dr Seuss’s ‘Cat in the Hat’ set for Hollywood adaptation
summary: The classic children’s book, which has sold over 16 million copies since 1957, is finally being turned into an animated feature film, complete with new character designs.

headline: US Democrats shift focus from culture wars to everyday issues
summary: During Donald Trump’s second term, the Democratic Party has reoriented its messaging toward kitchen-table concerns, moving away from previous emphasis on identity-based politics.

headline: Japan records first annual GDP contraction in a year
summary: Weak consumer spending and record-breaking rainfall have pushed Japan’s economy into contraction, complicating the central bank’s interest-rate strategy.

headline: Inquest examines role of birth keeper in newborn deaths
summary: An inquest into four infant deaths is scrutinising the actions of a midwife known as ‘Mumma Sita’, while a fundraising campaign seeks to cover her legal costs.

headline: Zelensky criticises SpaceX over alleged aid to Russia
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of providing Starlink services that may be assisting Russian attacks, as Washington urges Ukraine to consider territorial concessions for NATO membership.

headline: NSW police offer $500,000 reward for 2012 homicide case
summary: Police in New South Wales have announced a half-million-dollar reward for information leading to the resolution of a decade-old murder investigation involving Marlon McDonald, who vanished in 2012.

headline: Labor and Coalition pour cash into marginal seats
summary: Analysis shows the Coalition is targeting Labor-held must-win electorates with heavy spending, while Labor focuses resources on seats such as Ben Carroll’s to retain furniture. The funding battle highlights the intensity of the upcoming federal election campaign.

headline: Three Makybe Diva Melbourne Cup trophies stolen
summary: Three trophies won by legendary racehorse Makybe Diva were taken from a glass case at Flemington Racecourse. The owner described the loss as devastating and appealed for the trophies to be returned intact.

headline: Canada says it may partner with Chinese automakers if US talks fail
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney told reporters Canada will move forward with Chinese car makers should US-Canada trade negotiations not preserve an integrated North American auto industry, ahead of his meeting with President Xi in Shenzhen.

headline: New York teen reunited with cat after building collapse
summary: Rescuers located a teen’s missing cat in the rubble of a collapsed apartment four days after the youngster’s public plea for help.

headline: AI-assisted cheating sparks exam scandal in South Korea
summary: A university-entrance exam in South Korea was marred by a student using artificial intelligence to cheat, prompting authorities to promise a crackdown ahead of the annual test.

headline: Adelaide driver hailed as hero after stopping stroke-stricken motorist
summary: A man in Adelaide was praised for quickly intervening and preventing a driver suffering a stroke from causing an accident while swerving across lanes.

headline: China confirms historic summit with US and Russia leaders
summary: President Xi confirmed a three-way summit with President Trump and President Putin, with agendas expected to cover nuclear non-proliferation, the Middle East conflict, trade policies and the Ukraine war.

headline: Jollibee’s Australian entry may signal government’s trade focus
summary: Filipino fast-food giant Jollibee announced plans to open stores in Australia, prompting analysis that the move could reflect the Albanese government’s broader trade and investment strategy.

headline: Wallabies’ backline under scrutiny after loss to Scotland
summary: A defeat to Scotland highlighted concerns over the Wallabies’ whole-back attack ahead of upcoming tests against Wales and the All Blacks, with critics questioning the unit’s effectiveness.

headline: Reece Walsh criticises Australian supporters after World Cup win
summary: Kangaroos star Reece Walsh delivered an impassioned post-match interview, questioning the behaviour of some Australian fans following his team’s victory over New Zealand.

headline: Locksley expands copper-gold resource at Greater Tottenham
summary: Locksley Resources announced a resource increase at its Greater Tottenham project in NSW to 110,000 tonnes of copper and 100,000 ounces of gold, with a drilling rig now on site testing extensions.

headline: Perth murder suspect appears in court for first time
summary: A 38-year-old man charged with murder over a shooting death in Perth’s outer southern suburbs attended court for his initial hearing.

headline: Melbourne Cup runner So You Are dies of colic
summary: Five-year-old racehorse So You Are, which finished eighth in the Melbourne Cup, died from severe colic thirteen days after the race, according to trainer Bjorn Baker.

headline: Microsoft outage halts Outlook, no compensation expected
summary: Millions of users were unable to access Outlook email on Friday, disrupting business operations, but Microsoft indicated it will not provide financial compensation for the productivity loss.

headline: Aureka completes $8.9M acquisition to become gold producer
summary: Aureka Limited has bought a Victorian gold mine and mill for $8.9 million, turning the company into a gold producer with positive monthly free cash flow and spare processing capacity.

headline: Hailstorm blankets Mudgee, giant hail warning issued for NSW
summary: A severe hailstorm hit Mudgee, leaving yards covered in hail that resembled snow drifts. A giant hail warning was also issued for north-east New South Wales.

headline: University of Melbourne exam platform fails, students forced to stop
summary: Hundreds of University of Melbourne students could not access the digital platform for final exams, prompting the university to abort the tests. The issue was blamed on third-party technical partners.

headline: Hells Angels member charged with threatening journalist Nick McKenzie
summary: Police allege 36-year-old Kane Montebello, a Hells Angels bikie, sent threatening, offensive and abusive text messages to investigative reporter Nick McKenzie.

headline: China’s October economic activity slows more than expected
summary: Data show a sharper decline in China’s economic activity for October, prompting Beijing to accelerate budget spending in an effort to counter weaker growth.

headline: Northern Territory teen charged over alleged massacre plot
summary: A 14-year-old boy was charged with terrorism-related offences after allegedly planning a massacre at several locations, including a church, and possessing an Al-Qaeda training manual on his computer.

headline: Former defence employee deemed high-risk after weapons cache found
summary: A former defence employee who stored a weapons cache at his Adelaide home was found to be becoming radicalised and now faces strict conditions, including a ban on extremist activities.

headline: Coles investigates cyber-attack, urges customers to update passwords
summary: Australia’s second-largest retailer confirmed a cyber-attack on its systems. No customer, staff or supplier data was found compromised, but the company advised shoppers to change passwords and stay vigilant while investigations continue with the Australian Cyber Security Centre.

headline: Two stranded on Perth ferris wheel rescued after power cut
summary: Two people were left at the top of a 36-metre ferris wheel in Perth’s CBD after the ride was switched off. They used phone lights to signal rescuers before being safely brought down.

headline: Calls grow for Nvidia founder Jensen Huang to return as CEO
summary: Tech executives and major shareholders are urging Jensen Huang to resume his role as Nvidia chief executive following his resignation, citing concerns ahead of the company’s earnings report.

headline: Mexican drug lord Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo dies at 80
summary: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, the former head of the Guadalajara Cartel known as the ‘Boss of Bosses’, died at the age of 80.

headline: Tree felling begins for Adelaide MotoGP circuit amid protests
summary: Work has started to remove trees in Adelaide’s parklands to make way for a new MotoGP track, prompting dozens of protesters to gather at the site.

headline: Cisco forecasts AI infrastructure revenue to double this fiscal year
summary: Cisco reported earnings that beat expectations and said its AI infrastructure revenue is set to double over the current fiscal year as the company expands its AI-related offerings.

headline: WA music community upset over demolition of key all-ages venue
summary: The head of WA Music warned that the planned demolition of a popular all-ages venue is sending the state’s youth music scene sideways, adding uncertainty for a major upcoming youth music festival.

headline: Nvidia names new chair and CEO after founder’s exit amid scandal
summary: Nvidia has appointed Harvey Jones as chair and Colette Kress as chief executive to steady the chip maker following Jensen Huang’s sudden departure and a sex-scandal that has drawn attention to Chinese espionage concerns. The leadership change aims to restore investor confidence.

headline: Norway bans Russian and Belarusian athletes amid Ukraine war
summary: The Norwegian government announced a ban on Russian and Belarusian professional athletes competing in the country while the war in Ukraine continues, following a similar restriction recently introduced by Finland.

headline: Leeds woman admits stabbing murder of 16-year-old rival
summary: An 18-year-old woman pleaded guilty to murdering a 16-year-old girl in Leeds after a planned fight over a young man. The victim, Chloe Watson Dransfield, was stabbed at the suspect’s home. The court heard details of the incident and the relationship between the parties.

headline: Doctors urge redirect of gas hub funds to new Darwin hospital
summary: Medical groups in the Northern Territory are pressing Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to cancel funding for the Middle Arm gas hub precinct and reallocate the money to build a new Royal Darwin Hospital, arguing the health project is a higher priority.

headline: Bond yields jump to biggest surge since 2022 on Fed rate hike expectations
summary: U.S. bond yields surged to their largest increase since 2022 as markets priced in expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, following comments from Fed Chair Warsh that heightened volatility.

headline: Victorian government freezes emergency services levy for farmers
summary: The Victorian Labor Party has pledged to permanently freeze the emergency services tax rate for farmers, while opposition parties have promised to scrap the levy entirely, aiming to ease cost pressures on the agricultural sector.

headline: Trump says US no longer needs Iran peace agreement
summary: President Donald Trump indicated that the United States does not require a deal with Tehran, directing his nominee JD Vance to focus on domestic issues rather than pursuing the Iran nuclear agreement.

headline: United Airlines warns against AI agents booking flights
summary: United Airlines says its system will not allow AI agents to book flights, and an expert cautions that decisions involving health, wealth and privacy should still involve human input rather than fully automated bots.

headline: Greta Thunberg slams Australia's climate action
summary: Climate activist Greta Thunberg criticised Australia’s slow progress on climate policy when asked about the country’s record, highlighting the gap between its emissions targets and actual measures.

headline: ‘False crops’ technique targets invasive red witchweed
summary: Researchers are using a ‘false crops’ method to trick the invasive red witchweed into self-destruction, the only known infestation of the weed was first identified in Habana in 2013.

headline: Two men charged after nail gun road-rage incident on M1
summary: Police have charged two men following an alleged road-rage episode on the M1 Princes Motorway where a nail fired from a ute struck an SUV driver’s face before the vehicles collided.

headline: Ukrainian drone strikes Russian warship in Gulf of Finland
summary: A Ukrainian drone attacked a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, marking the first known strike on a Russian vessel in open Baltic waters, raising tensions in the region.

headline: Sixers prevail as Ellyse Perry run-out sparks debate
summary: The Sydney Sixers won their WBBL match despite a controversial run-out of star all-rounder Ellyse Perry, after a replay on the big screen prompted umpires to overturn the original decision.

headline: South Australia permits gas use for data centre power
summary: The South Australian government gave approval for gas to be used in powering data centres, stating it is acceptable despite the state’s renewable-energy strategy, aiming to support the sector’s growth.

headline: Home affairs minister weighs backtrack on backpacker visa changes
summary: Minister Tony Burke is considering reversing the government’s recent backpacker visa policy announced two months ago, amid ongoing debate over its impact on the sector.

headline: Kalshi ends advisory role for Donald Trump Jr amid political scrutiny
summary: Prediction-market platform Kalshi announced that Donald Trump Jr is no longer a paid adviser, describing the split as a mutual business decision. The move follows the former president’s investment firm increasing its stake in rival Polymarket, prompting Democrats to signal investigations into Trump family investments.

headline: AFLW star says she won’t settle as Hawthorn eye semi-final
summary: AFLW player Jenna Richardson says she does not want to settle, as her Hawthorn side prepares for a semi-final rematch against Carlton.

headline: Only four ministers achieve net savings this year
summary: An analysis shows that out of all government ministers, only four have recorded net savings so far this year as the administration pushes cost-cutting ahead of the mid-year budget update.

headline: Midwife to halve caseload under new homebirth scheme
summary: Jenny Spencer says a new federal insurance scheme that only covers some private midwives for homebirth will force her to cut her client list in half, limiting access to homebirth services.

headline: US Treasury to hire debt collectors for student-loan defaults
summary: The Treasury Department proposes paying debt collectors reduced fees to pursue borrowers who have defaulted on student loans, marking the first such hiring in six years.

headline: Department store decline reshapes future of shopping
summary: Analysts examine how the fading of traditional department stores and the rise of online trade could affect physical retail spaces and consumer habits moving forward.

headline: Seniors, carers cards to move onto Service Queensland app
summary: Queensland's state government will add seniors, carers and companion cards to the Service Queensland app, prompting concerns about increased digitisation of essential services.

headline: David Jones store closures linked to outer-suburb financial strain
summary: Experts say the financial pressure in outer suburbs contributed to David Jones' decision to shut 19 stores, ending a 188-year retail legacy.

headline: Four Victorians named in Australian of the Year awards
summary: Four individuals from Victoria have been announced as nominees for the Australian of the Year awards, including a pancreatic cancer advocate whose late husband played for the Hawks.

headline: Fed to skip interest-rate vote at October 2027 meeting
summary: The US Federal Reserve announced that its October 2027 policy meeting will be a non-voting session, providing extra time for deliberation without a formal rate decision or post-meeting statement. Seven voting meetings are planned for the next year.

headline: Geelong residents decry unfulfilled election promises
summary: A Geelong mother says the city has seen promised projects scrapped, delayed or ignored, raising concerns that voters may punish parties that fail to deliver on election pledges.

headline: Nearly 2,000 tonnes of farmed salmon die in Tasmania’s Macquarie Harbour
summary: Data shows almost 2,000 tonnes of farmed salmon perished over a 15-month period in Macquarie Harbour on Tasmania’s west coast, prompting calls for investigation into the cause of the mass mortality.

headline: Brisbane ferry terminal closure sparks anger among commuters and retailers
summary: The shutdown of a busy ferry terminal in Brisbane has left commuters scrambling for alternatives and local businesses reporting lost sales, describing the temporary arrangements as a “schemozzle”.

headline: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow to discuss peace prospects
summary: US representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with President Vladimir Putin in Moscow as part of renewed diplomatic efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

headline: Building collapse in Brooklyn kills eight, including two children
summary: A residential building in Brooklyn, New York, collapsed, killing eight people – two children and six adults – and injuring 18 others, with rescue crews working amid dangerous conditions.

headline: Woman shot in leg at Western Sydney home
summary: Police responded to a domestic incident in Western Sydney where a woman sustained a gunshot wound to the leg. The investigation is ongoing.

headline: Hegseth receives medal after reprimanding guard at war memorial
summary: Specialist Thomas Iglesias was awarded a medal after he shouted at a group for being noisy at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, an incident that drew public attention.

headline: Jobless Australians face uncertain next steps
summary: A SBS feature outlines the challenges Australians encounter after losing employment, highlighting the financial and emotional hurdles that often follow a job loss.

headline: UK ministers consider tightening NDA rules after Walliams allegations
summary: The British government is reviewing legislation to restrict the use of non-disclosure agreements following a Guardian investigation into harassment claims involving TV personality David Walliams.

headline: Sydney artist Nick Ward releases experimental new album
summary: Nick Ward, once tipped as the next Troye Sivan, launches a messy, unconventional album that showcases his evolving artistic direction.

headline: Lewis Hamilton calls Gaza situation a genocide
summary: Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton described the situation in Gaza as a genocide after visiting the Rafah border crossing. He urged Israel to allow aid trucks into Gaza, citing briefings he received from aid workers during his trip.

headline: Super accounts not guaranteed against hacking theft
summary: The Australian government does not guarantee superannuation accounts if they are stolen in a cyber-attack, though some coverage may still apply. The article clarifies common misconceptions about protection for super funds in the event of a hack.

headline: AI firms could turn Australia into copyright tax haven
summary: Former competition regulator Rod Sims warned that global AI companies may seek to exploit Australia as a low-tax hub for large-scale content theft. He highlighted concerns that the sector could attract firms looking to minimise copyright-related taxes.

headline: Housing minister Clare O’Neil linked to falling house prices
summary: Housing Minister Clare O’Neil is portrayed as a ‘change agent’ amid the decline in Australian house prices. The piece examines whether the government should claim credit for the market downturn and the policy steps being considered.

headline: Weight-loss drug retatrutide may relieve knee pain
summary: Large-scale trials of the GLP-1 drug retatrutide suggest it can reduce knee pain in osteoarthritis patients. Researchers observed pain relief but remain uncertain about the underlying mechanism, noting the potential dual benefit of weight loss and joint comfort.

headline: Greens push for public naming of trust beneficiaries
summary: The Greens are demanding that beneficiaries of discretionary trusts be publicly disclosed as part of a deal to support Labor’s budget plan to impose a 30% tax on such trusts. They argue transparency will aid tax fairness.

headline: EV and battery subsidies face review, Bowen says
summary: Energy Minister Chris Bowen confirmed that Australia’s electric-vehicle and home-battery subsidy programmes are under review, but he ruled out an immediate withdrawal of support. The review aims to assess the schemes’ effectiveness amid fiscal pressures.

headline: Doctors warn of recurring critical drug shortages
summary: Australian doctors have highlighted frequent shortages of essential medicines, pointing to supply-chain weaknesses that could worsen. The analysis underscores the need for stronger procurement and inventory strategies to ensure reliable access to critical drugs.

headline: Australians keep spending despite cost-of-living pressure
summary: Many Australians continue to spend on non-essential items even as they feel the pinch of a cost-of-living crunch. Analysts suggest the behaviour reflects deeper psychological factors rather than pure irrationality.

headline: Rupert Murdoch appears at New York event
summary: Media mogul Rupert Murdoch made a high-profile appearance at a New York function, after which former employee Siobhan McKenna hosted a farewell gathering before departing for the same city.

headline: Metricon relocates head office to Ferntree Business Park
summary: Australia’s largest home builder Metricon is shifting its headquarters to Ferntree Business Park in Notting Hill, expanding its footprint as it continues to grow its national presence.

headline: Heritage home demolition sparks controversy in inner west
summary: The demolition of a turn-of-the-century house in Sydney’s inner west has provoked public outcry and reignited debate over heritage protection versus housing development.

headline: Usman Khawaja’s Sandpapergate revelations reignite cricket scandal debate
summary: Former Australian captain Usman Khawaja’s disclosures about the Sandpapergate incident have resurfaced, prompting renewed scrutiny of the cricket board’s handling of the controversy eight years on.

headline: Duran Duran drummer Roger Taylor quits over worsening tinnitus
summary: Roger Taylor, the long-standing drummer for Duran Duran, announced his departure from the band, citing severe tinnitus that forces him to prioritise his health.

headline: German military grounds Quantum Systems drones after cyber attack
summary: German armed forces have grounded drones from start-up Quantum Systems following a cyber-attack, marking the latest European defence firm to face security breaches.

headline: Putin warns US of targeting foreign troops as Starlink disruptions continue
summary: President Vladimir Putin told US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine, while also noting renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink service for Ukrainian forces.

headline: US home sales drop to lowest level since 2010
summary: US home sales have fallen to their lowest level since 2010 as higher mortgage rates curb buyer demand. The slowdown reflects the impact of rising borrowing costs on the housing market, deepening the existing slump in transactions.

headline: IRS raises 2027 401(k) contribution limits
summary: The US Internal Revenue Service announced higher contribution caps for 401(k) plans in 2027, allowing savers to increase their retirement savings.

summary: At the UN climate summit in Antalya, Greta Thunberg accused world leaders of killing the planet, urging stronger action to halt environmental breakdown.

summary: October home sales fell to the lowest level since the Great Recession, with buyers retreating amid 7 % mortgage rates and all-time high property prices, marking a sharp slowdown in the market.

summary: Delray Beach announced the cancellation of its popular St Patrick’s Day parade to comply with a new Florida law that bars municipalities from hosting events deemed to promote diversity, equity and inclusion, sparking public outrage.

headline: Gunman kills one and injures four in Washington DC shooting
summary: A shooter opened fire near the White House, killing a person at a gym and wounding four others. Police later contained the suspect, who shot himself. The incident shifted from an active-shooter response to a barricaded-subject operation, with authorities urging residents to stay indoors.

summary: Legislation under consideration would lower the Medicare eligibility age from 65 to 50, extending coverage to about 60 million American workers. The proposal, distinct from Medicare-for-All, aims to broaden health security for mid-career adults.

headline: Disney partners with Cosm to bring Star Wars to dome theatres
summary: Cosm secured a multi-year film deal with Disney, bringing "Star Wars: A New Hope" and future titles to its dome venues as part of a broader collaboration.

headline: Yankees chief backs college sports legislation, discusses MLB talks
summary: New York Yankees president Randy Levine urged support for the Protect College Sports Act, which would allow athletes to profit from their name, image and likeness. He also commented on ongoing labour negotiations between Major League Baseball and the players’ union, highlighting the sport’s economic challenges.

headline: European leaders reject Russian push to overhaul continent’s security
summary: EU heads pushed back against Moscow’s proposal to revamp European security structures, with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy warning of heightened risks as talks continue in Abu Dhabi.

headline: Nebius shares tumble 16% after weak 2026 capex outlook
summary: Nebius fell 16 % on the market after issuing a cautious outlook for 2026 capital expenditure, lagging behind peers IREN and CoreWeave that posted stronger recent results.

headline: MSF says millions of Ebola aid funds missing, staff unpaid
summary: Médecins Sans Frontières warned that large sums of Ebola relief money are unaccounted for, leaving medical staff without pay, training or essential supplies as the virus continues to spread.

headline: Employer-backed home purchases rise as housing affordability worsens
summary: A MarketWatch survey notes an increase in first-time buyers receiving financial assistance from their employers, highlighting the growing difficulty of purchasing a home even for those with stable jobs.

headline: Oil prices mixed after Trump says Iran deal not needed
summary: Crude futures moved sideways on Thursday following President Donald Trump’s comments that a U.S.–Iran agreement was unnecessary, sparking concerns the conflict could continue.

summary: A CNBC analysis shows that although mortgage rates were 7 % in 1997, today’s typical home consumes a much larger share of household earnings, making home buying feel more expensive despite similar rates.

summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia chief executive after an affair with an employee alleged to be a Chinese spy. Shares fell up to 10%, wiping tens of billions from market value. Colette Kress was named interim CEO and Huang’s $140 billion stake, held jointly with his wife, adds uncertainty.

summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage featured on Russell Brand’s US podcast, condemning the Labour party for “cosying up” to the comedian after Brand’s recent sexual-assault conviction.

summary: UKHSA says only 28% of 18- and 19-year-olds have received the first dose in a one-off campaign, amid an outbreak that caused three deaths and serious illness.

summary: President Trump says levies will increase if Mexico does not curb illegal crossings, signalling a possible escalation in trade tensions.

headline: Two men convicted of aiding Iran in plot against UK journalists
summary: Men of Iranian origin were found guilty of conducting surveillance for Tehran’s intelligence services to facilitate violence against UK-based journalists between 2024 and 2025.

headline: Australian federal police warn of surge in teen extremist material
summary: AFP says 32 of 37 youths prosecuted for extremist offences were charged in the past two years, with many found possessing “hard drives full of gore”.

headline: New allegations emerge against convicted rapist Ralph Carr
summary: Former staffers detail unwanted sexual advances by Melbourne talent manager Ralph Carr, who was previously found guilty of raping an ex-employee.

headline: NSW ICAC report highlights ‘guns for hire’ issue, calls for reform
summary: The corruption watchdog’s inquiry reveals ease of undeclared lobbying and gun-for-hire problems, criticising both major parties for inaction on recommended reforms.

headline: NSW Labor runs 'news' Instagram account, raising communication law concerns
summary: A new Instagram account presenting itself as an independent news source is being operated by the NSW Labor party. Experts warn it exploits a loophole in political communication rules, as the state government and other parties also use similar unaffiliated accounts to share partisan content.

headline: Eight killed in Colombian air strike on Gulf Clan gang
summary: A Colombian air strike targeting the Gulf Clan gang resulted in eight deaths, including a high-profile gang leader identified as a priority target by the president.

headline: Poundland granted two-week extension to secure buyer
summary: UK discount retailer Poundland has received a high-court order extending its creditor protection by two weeks while it seeks a new owner. The move gives the chain, which employs about 12,000 staff, more time to evaluate bids from three potential purchasers.

headline: UK proposes ending criminal record checks for youth offences
summary: The government plans to stop requiring employers to see criminal records of people convicted of offences committed under the age of 18. Ministers say the change will help reduce youth incarceration and improve employment prospects for disadvantaged young people in England and Wales.

headline: Record credit-card balances raise risk of hidden medical-debt
summary: U.S. consumers have pushed credit-card debt to a new high, and experts warn that mounting medical bills are increasingly being added to cards, creating “shadow debt” that is harder to track and could strain household finances.

headline: Zimbabwe author cleared after AI plagiarism probe
summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza has been exonerated following a month-long investigation that confirmed his Caine prize-winning short story was written by a human, ending allegations that artificial intelligence was used.

headline: Unions claim credit for Democratic wins in 2026 midterms
summary: Labor unions say their multi-million-dollar spending and member mobilisation helped Democrats secure major victories in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, and are now urging the party to deliver concrete policy actions.

headline: UK economy outperforms expectations amid AI boost
summary: Analysts note that the UK has posted its fastest growth in over two years, driven in part by artificial-intelligence adoption. Despite concerns over a tech slowdown and rising energy costs, the economy expanded by 0.7% in the latest quarter, defying earlier forecasts.

headline: Ukraine power plant operates under constant drone threat
summary: One of Ukraine’s largest power stations, heavily damaged by a Russian missile strike, remains functional but faces ongoing danger from drone attacks, highlighting the precarious state of the country’s energy infrastructure.

headline: Australian quantum start-up Q-CTRL reaches unicorn status
summary: Q-CTRL, a home-grown quantum-technology company, has been valued at over $1 billion after raising $420 million, expanding its portfolio from quantum-software tools to a navigation system developed with Airbus.

headline: Petrol prices fall as global oil costs drop 20%
summary: Australian motorists are seeing lower pump prices after crude oil prices slipped by about one-fifth this month, providing temporary relief for drivers facing high fuel expenses.

headline: Metro Bank puts itself up for sale, billionaire eyes £420m windfall
summary: Metro Bank announced it is seeking bids after three years since its rescue, with Colombian billionaire Jaime Gilinski Bacal expected to reap a £420 million gain if the sale proceeds, sending the share price up 7%.

headline: Bomb hoax threats trigger evacuations at Italian schools
summary: Schools across Italy faced fresh evacuations after receiving bomb threats for a second consecutive day, causing panic among students and staff.

headline: OECD reports migration to rich countries falls for second year
summary: The OECD says inflows to wealthy nations declined for a second year as stricter visa rules limit workers, students and refugees moving abroad.

headline: Meta restores Australian Femicide Watch page
summary: Meta has reinstated the Femicide Watch page that tracks murders of women in Australia after founder Sherele Moody requested its revival.

headline: Israel attack on Gaza hospital kills six despite ceasefire
summary: An Israeli strike on the Nasser medical complex in Gaza killed six people, including doctors and patients, despite a declared ceasefire.

headline: Milburn review proposes cuts to youth welfare benefits in UK
summary: Former Labour minister Alan Milburn's review recommends reducing welfare payments for young people not in education, employment or training. The proposal could represent the biggest overhaul of the UK benefits system in a decade, aiming to address rising numbers of NEETs and reshape the welfare landscape.

headline: Manchester United dismiss Carrick as manager
summary: Manchester United have sacked former midfielder Michael Carrick after a ten-month tenure that left the club in the relegation zone. The club said a change was necessary to achieve its ambitions for the season.

headline: Former DJ Tim Westwood denies additional sexual offence charges
summary: Ex-Radio 1 presenter Tim Westwood appeared in court to deny two further sexual offence charges, bringing the total to 17 alleged offences spanning 1983 to 2016. He entered not-guilty pleas for all charges.

headline: Far-right activist admits damaging Channel dinghy
summary: Daniel Thomas, a far-right activist, changed his plea to guilty on a single charge of criminal damage after slashing a dinghy with a knife in the Channel. He continues to deny a separate charge of failing to disclose a phone PIN to police.

headline: Strategist warns against chasing tech stock bounce
summary: Jim Thorne, chief market strategist at Wellington-Altus Private Wealth, cautioned investors not to be lured into a rapid rebound in tech stocks, describing the potential bounce as "violent" but urging restraint until fundamentals improve.

headline: Scout Motors nears completion of South Carolina plant with 212,000 reservations
summary: Scout Motors reported roughly 212,000 reservations for its Terra pickup and Traveler SUV as its $2 billion manufacturing facility in South Carolina approaches completion, signalling strong consumer interest ahead of the vehicle launch.

headline: Burberry posts profit as sales surge in China and US
summary: Luxury fashion house Burberry returned to profit, driven by a 6% sales increase across coats, jackets and handbags. Strong online and wholesale performance in China and the United States underpinned the growth, which CEO Joshua Schulman credited to a back-to-basics strategy.

headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza's Nasser hospital, killing six
summary: An Israeli missile struck Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, Gaza, killing six people including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounding more than 20. The health ministry said the building housed surgical wards and intensive care units. Israel said it targeted Hamas fighters but offered no evidence.

headline: Ukraine reports Starshield satellite disruptions amid US-Russia talks
summary: Ukraine's president said recent speed restrictions on the Starshield military satellite network were hindering its defence efforts. The concerns were raised as US envoys arrived in Moscow for talks with President Putin, highlighting tensions over the technology's reliability in the ongoing conflict.

headline: Euclid mission maps 900 million galaxies in first data release
summary: The European Space Agency’s Euclid telescope released its inaugural dataset, revealing more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 gravitational-lensing candidates. The mission aims to produce the largest three-dimensional map of the universe, covering a third of the sky and tracing cosmic history back over 10 billion years.

headline: Five new miniature frog species discovered in eastern Himalayas
summary: Scientists have identified five previously unknown miniature frog species in the eastern Himalayas. The research suggests the frogs evolved alongside the uplift of the mountain range and the development of the Asian monsoon, highlighting the region’s unique biodiversity and geological history.

headline: College students rally across US campuses to back Starbucks boycott
summary: Students, staff and elected officials gathered at more than 40 US colleges to support the Starbucks Workers United boycott. The campaign seeks higher pay, a $17-hour minimum wage and a three-person staffing minimum, after five years of stalled contract talks with the coffee chain.

headline: John Kerry calls Trump ‘biggest loser’ over climate policy at COP31
summary: Speaking at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey, former US secretary of state John Kerry criticised former President Donald Trump for withdrawing the United States from climate commitments and handing the clean-energy lead to China, saying the move makes Trump the biggest loser in the climate arena.

headline: NHS England removes claim that 137 trusts benefit from Palantir AI
summary: After The Guardian exposed that only 29 NHS trusts were using Palantir’s AI data platform, NHS England deleted a website statement that had claimed 137 trusts were benefiting from the technology, acknowledging the earlier information was misleading.

headline: Maga architects blame Big Tech and AI data centres for US midterms loss
summary: The Heritage Foundation’s head argued that the Republican Party’s embrace of Silicon Valley and the fallout from the US-Iran war contributed to their defeat in the recent midterm elections, linking tech-sector policies to voter backlash.

headline: Ukraine says Starlink restrictions reinstated as US envoys arrive in Moscow
summary: Ukraine reported that restrictions on SpaceX’s Starlink service have been re-imposed, coinciding with a visit by US officials to Moscow. The move follows heightened tensions over Russian drone activity and diplomatic talks involving senior US figures.

headline: Greta Thunberg criticises Australia’s net-zero progress at COP31
summary: At the COP31 summit in Turkey, climate activist Greta Thunberg slammed Australia’s pace on net-zero emissions, describing it as slower than a snail. Her remarks drew a large media presence and prompted security guards to escort her from the stage.

headline: The return of the snatch-and-grab state
summary: A new historical analysis examines how modern governments employ confiscation tactics as a form of economic warfare, reviving the concept of the snatch-and-grab state in contemporary policy debates.

headline: Anti-AI trade measures boost Indian equities, analysts say
summary: Research suggests that the worst anti-AI trade policies by major chipmakers correlate with stronger performance of Indian stocks, highlighting a potential investment angle as global tech regulation intensifies.

headline: Italy proposes exit tax on emigrants’ capital gains
summary: The Italian government has introduced a tax targeting capital gains of wealthy emigrants, aiming to capture revenue from assets moved abroad. While theoretically sound, officials acknowledge challenges in practical implementation.

headline: Floreat gunman’s recording revealed at inquest into murders
summary: During the inquest into the deaths of Jennifer and Gretl Petelcyzc, evidence emerged that the Floreat shooter inadvertently recorded himself on the day of the attack, shedding new light on his interactions with police prior to the incident.

headline: Australia to spend $80m on workforce for AUKUS
summary: The Australian government will allocate more than $80 million to expand training pathways and build a skilled workforce capable of supporting the AUKUS defence partnership, aiming to attract workers at all career stages and boost domestic capability for the submarine project.

headline: UK drone maker UForce valued at £4.5bn after £500m fundraise
summary: London-based naval drone company UForce, founded by Ukrainian entrepreneurs, reached a £4.5 billion valuation after raising over £500 million, including a £113 million investment from the UK’s national wealth fund, making it one of the country’s fastest-growing unicorns with equipment used extensively in the Ukraine war.

headline: Government provider breach may have exposed personal details
summary: A government-run service provider disclosed that a cyber breach could have compromised personal information, including contact details, of individuals whose data it holds, prompting an investigation and advice for affected users to monitor for potential misuse.

headline: Italy’s anti-vax doctors seek return to frontline amid political push
summary: A group of Italian doctors stripped of their licences for anti-vaccination views are lobbying for reinstatement, with support from far-right politician Roberto Vannacci, as the debate intensifies ahead of the 2027 elections and raises questions about medical staffing and public health policy.

headline: 72-year-old British woman missing from cruise ship in Atlantic
summary: A 72-year-old British passenger vanished from the Tui cruise liner as it sailed towards the Caribbean, prompting a search operation by authorities and the cruise line while family members appeal for information on her whereabouts.

headline: Mayoral candidates propose reforms to curb council toxicity
summary: Candidates vying for mayoral office have suggested measures such as reducing council representatives, appointing an external auditor and tightening meeting discipline to address reports of a toxic, bullying culture within the local council and restore public confidence.

headline: Prince Harry and Meghan settle in new Cotswolds home
summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have moved into a new residence on a friend’s estate in the Cotswolds, following their return to the United Kingdom with their children earlier this year, according to reports.

headline: Senator Cotton urges US ban on Chinese memory chip maker CXMT
summary: US Senator Tom Cotton has called on the Commerce Department to place Chinese DRAM producer CXMT on the Entity List, citing national-security concerns as the company expands its memory-chip production and moves into high-bandwidth memory markets.

headline: Ex-bureaucrat says minister likely struck CFMEU deal over complaint line
summary: A former senior public servant testified to a Queensland inquiry that the former minister probably reached an agreement with the construction union CFMEU concerning a complaint-handling line, describing the arrangement as a logical conclusion to the regulator’s backtrack on union-friendly policies.

headline: Labuschagne’s aggressive batting fuels call for Webster’s recall
summary: Former Australian all-rounder believes Labuschagne’s energetic performance with the ball could trigger a resurgence and support a recall for veteran spinner Webster.

headline: Social-media app seen as key voter influencer in Ringwood
summary: The Chinese-Australian community in Melbourne’s east holds considerable voting power, urging politicians to recognise its diversity and long memory ahead of the Victorian election.

headline: Ukrainian drone startup UFORCE valued at $6 billion
summary: UFORCE, a defence-tech startup, reached a $6 billion valuation as investors back its battle-tested drones and naval vessels that have logged hundreds of thousands of combat flights.

headline: Liberal party urges big business to look after itself
summary: Liberal MP Tim Wilson told big firms they must fend for themselves, arguing the Coalition still owes small businesses for its handling of the pandemic.

headline: Coalition lacks climate policy as debate shifts
summary: The opposition argues the Coalition has moved from a developed climate policy to none, while Labor claims it is on the right side of history.

headline: Universities face domestic caps, urged to cut overseas fee reliance
summary: Tertiary education chief Barney Glover warned universities they must secure futures without depending on lucrative international student fees after domestic enrolment caps are imposed.

headline: Community opposition to data-centre expansion cited as democratic pushback
summary: Advocates say data centres will keep NSW at the technological forefront, but local residents argue the boom should not come at the expense of their suburbs.

headline: Sam Konstas scores century, pressures NSW Test selectors
summary: Konstas’s latest hundred for New South Wales in the Sheffield Shield puts Test selectors under pressure to consider him for the national side.

headline: Bikie gang violence targets Brighton property developer
summary: A violent campaign by a bikie gang against developer Simon Pitard resulted in an innocent couple being caught in the crossfire at their Cheltenham home.

headline: Storm damage forces school closures across Brisbane

headline: VCAA website hacked, alleged sale of exam papers
summary: The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority’s website was compromised during the state’s exam period. A hacker using the alias “DaggerElite” claimed to have sold VCE exam papers to hundreds of students, though officials say no evidence of a leak exists.

headline: Milburn review proposes cuts to under-25s welfare benefits
summary: A government-commissioned review led by Chris Milburn recommends moving people under 25 off the main sickness-benefit system, signalling a major overhaul of Australia’s welfare framework for younger recipients.

headline: Police link organised thefts to Shepparton shoplifting blitz
summary: Victoria police say a coordinated operation targeting repeat offenders behind a wave of retail thefts in Shepparton has resulted in more than 200 arrests, highlighting organised crime in regional Australia.

headline: Weinstein’s ex-assistant comments on Walliams allegations
summary: Britain’s culture secretary cites the allegations against comedian David Walliams as part of a broader pattern of power abuse in the entertainment industry, referencing insights from Harvey Weinstein’s former assistant.
